questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A central reason for choosing UCD in Dublin was the strong academic reputation of the university and the range of courses offered within my field of study. I wanted to study at a university where I could strengthen my academic profile while experiencing a different teaching style and an international learning environment.
Dublin was also an attractive destination because it is an English-speaking city, which gave me the opportunity to improve my academic and everyday English. In addition, I was interested in experiencing Irish culture, meeting new people from different countries, and living in a vibrant student city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was a little difficult to find the information I needed upon arrival. Although some information was available, I often felt that I had to figure things out on my own and actively search for answers myself.
The first period required a lot of independence, especially when it came to practical matters and understanding how things worked at the university. However, over time it became easier as I got more familiar with the systems, the campus, and who to contact for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The student desk was very helpful, along with our module coordinater, Jana.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Some different types of accommodation, all of them sharing apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen is completely empty when you arrive, you have to bring/buy everything yourself (tableware, pan, pot, etc.)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You are living with three other students, no oven in the kitchen (unless you pay a lot more for the more expensive apartments).

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UCD use different websites, UCD Connect, UCD Global (especially for Erasmus) SISWeb and Brightspace.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Everything, they have a lot of different phone numbers for different issues.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the classes/modules that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure the classes you take, are at the right level corresponding to your home university. I had a class/module that was way too hard and too different from what I was used to.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level 3 and 4

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mainly lectures like I was used to at UCPH, some classes and practicals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PHAR30110-Cardiovascular & Renal Disease, BIOC40220-Hot topics in Biochemistry, PHAR30030-Toxicology and BMOL40330-Biomol. Sci. Research Project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The courses PHAR30030-Toxicology and BIOC40220-Hot topics in Biochemistry was very good and relevant for the pharmacy study. 
BMOL40330-Biomol. Sci. Research Project was my bachelor which I was so happy to be a part of in Dr Monica de Gaetano's lab group. 
The course PHAR30110-Cardiovascular & Renal Disease was a medicine course and a lot different from pharmacy. I think the exam was too difficult and medicine focused, compared to what we learn as pharmacy students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can think of seriously. A lot of societies (from harry potter society to indian society to film society), clubs, three gyms, a swimmingpool, the clubhouse (bar).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Film society (it only costs 2€ and they show the newest movies and you'll have free popcorn and soda) and ESN society (also only 2€ and 10% of Ryanair flights and much more)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Galway, Belfast, Glendalough/Wicklow Mountains, watch a Gaelic football or Hurling match in a big stadium, travel to Edinburgh, visit pubs

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it's a lot similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How sweet and welcoming they all are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You will definitely be the oldest as a undergraduate, go out during the week days, be early if you want to study at the library (go to Health Science Library instead of Joyce, always space)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be a part of a real laboratory group, making experiments and getting results that actually matters. You learn a lot being a part of a team.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think speaking english, at least tuning in on how irish-english sounds. Don't underestimate how much energy you spend on learning and listening in english.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
